newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SNB confirms foundation plan hinges on gold sales.
newsitem.headline: SNB confirms foundation plan hinges on gold sales.

text.p: The Swiss National Bank (SNB) reconfirmed on Thursday that Switzerland's plan to finance a seven billion Swiss franc humanitarian fund for victims of the Holocaust and other tragedies hinged on selling gold from official reserves.

SNB Chairman Hans Meyer said on Wednesday that the planned foundation would be financed with a substantial proportion of revaluation gains achieved on SNB gold reserves, now valued at the fixed legal parity of 4,595 francs per kg.

"On the basis of a more realistic -- albeit still cautious -- valuation, several billion francs could be transferred in gold to the foundation," Meyer said, permitting investments yielding several hundred million francs a year annually.
"It is envisioned that the foundation would sell the gold transferred to it in the market over a period of approximately 10 years and invest the proceeds in interest-bearing assets," he said.
"In view of the modest annual volume of such sales and given a prudent approach, which is in the foundation's own interest, this should be possible without market disruption," he added.
Asked this correctly reflected the SNB's position, an spokesman said on Thursday: "That is right".
The foundation must still clear several legal hurdles and could take as long as two years to establish, officials said. Opponents may also mount a referendum drive to try to block it.
